subject: Private/on-prem feasibility: runtime constraints, resourcing, and cost coverage
messages:

Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, sales@opsinfra.com, hannah@turingcloud.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private/on-prem feasibility: runtime constraints, resourcing, and cost coverage

Team / partners —

Following up from yesterday's sync: attached is an initial feasibility estimate (private-deploy-estimate-v1.pdf) and a resourcing workbook (resourcing-estimates-apr10.xlsx). Goal: a tight read on what we need to commit to run a typical inference workload for TuringCloud's pilot (50 qps, median gen length 128 tokens, 99th-pct latency target < 250ms).

Key asks (please respond inline or in the doc):
- Architecture: what runtime constraints should we bake into the pilot SOW? (network egress limits, KMS boundary, allowed quantization levels)
- Resourcing: how many GPUs (and which class) + expected ops headcount for 24/7 SLA during pilot?
- Cost coverage: does TuringCloud sign a partial infrastructure reimbursement or do we price into Redwood Dedicated credits?
- Risk: upfront list of any blocking infra items that would push us to a cloud-only pilot.

Notes: the pilot must run inside the customer's VPC with customer-controlled KMS keys. We should assume they want private control plane (no traffic through our public control plane) and may require SOC2 evidence for audit. OpsInfra is looped for network/topology questions and a rough deployment timeline for bare-metal and cloud-hosted private options.

Next step: compile answers by EOD Monday 4/12 so Marissa can finalize the pilot SOW. If you need a short working session, propose 30 minutes and I'll coordinate.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Program Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: private-deploy-estimate-v1.pdf (summary); resourcing-estimates-apr10.xlsx (breakdown by role and hours)

Subject: Re: Private/on-prem feasibility: runtime constraints, resourcing, and cost coverage

Avery — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Two fast clarifications from product: 

1) SLA scope: for pilot we want an operational SLO of 99.9% per-week availability and best-effort latency targets (we can list absolute SLOs in SOW later). For pricing I want a clear line between what we consider "configuration/installation" vs "ongoing inference hours".

2) Constraints: the pilot needs to support live reroute back to hosted models (fallback) if their private capacity is saturated. That implies we have to support encrypted egress to Redwood-hosted endpoints and mutual TLS. Is that feasible given the VPC-only requirement?

I'll review the numbers in the spreadsheet and call out anything that looks out-of-line. If OpsInfra can give a network/topology diagram and deployment timeline that would help.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Hi Avery / Marissa —

Thanks for looping us in. Quick technical notes from our side based on the stated workload (50 qps, 128 tokens median):
- Recommended baseline: 2x NVIDIA A100 80GB per availability zone for redundancy; for a small pilot we can size down to 1x A100 + 1x A40 if cost is constrained but latency variance increases.
- Network: we deploy via a transit VPC with two ENIs per host (control + data). For fully private control plane we can support customer-managed bastion + SSM tunnel; mutual TLS termination is supported at the edge pod.
- Storage & KV cache: recommend local NVMe for per-host KV caching; plan for 800GB usable cache per host for a 128-token median workload at our observed cache hit rates.
- Timeline: 3-4 weeks for cloud-hosted private (customer VPC in AWS); 6-9 weeks for on-prem bare-metal (procurement + racks).

We can produce a topology diagram (attached as a one-pager) and a short bill-of-materials.

Regards,
OpsInfra Sales
OpsInfra Inc.

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private/on-prem feasibility: runtime constraints, resourcing, and cost coverage

Team —

I pulled the spreadsheet and sketched a conservative engineering estimate. High level points: 

- Runtime constraints: to hit 99th-pct latency <250ms at 50 qps we will need to prioritize KV cache affinity and continuous batching. That implies we cannot over-shard models across too many small GPUs; prefer fewer high-memory GPUs to keep KV co-located.

- Memory: the 800GB NVMe recommendation from OpsInfra is fine; however expect 32-40GB RAM per worker for tokenization + model runtime state depending on quantization. If customer requires 8-bit only we save memory but add dequant overhead.

- Quantization: model quantization to 8-bit (q4/q8) is acceptable for most open models but we should keep a 16-bit variant for quality-sensitive routes. That affects storage and image management (we need an extra model image per quant level).

- Ops staffing: for a pilot with 2 AZs, estimate 0.4 FTE SRE during onboarding (4 weeks), then 0.15 FTE ongoing (on-call rotations shared across customers). If we provide 24/7 coverage as an add-on, that's +1.0 FTE for the pilot period.

- GPU-hours: approx 3,600 GPU-hours/month for steady 50 qps on A100-80 (rough estimate in spreadsheet). If we use batching aggressively that could drop by ~25%.

Blocking items I see: mutual TLS egress to Redwood-hosted fallback requires a cert rotation plan and KMS integration work (customer KMS -> our control plane exchange). If customer insists on no egress whatsoever, we need a hardened local fallback model set and clear roll-forward plan.

I'll add a tab with the engineering assumptions to the spreadsheet. Recommend a short architecture walkthrough with OpsInfra and their network team before finalizing SOW.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
